lines.japanese: 俺たちは目を開けた。
lines.english: We opened our eyes.

lines.japanese: 朝だった。
lines.english: It was morning.

lines.japanese: だが、ただの朝ではなかった。
lines.english: But it was no ordinary morning.

lines.japanese: ものすごく朝だった。
lines.english: It was morning with a vengeance.

lines.japanese: 従来比五倍の朝だ。
lines.english: Five times as much morning as before.

lines.japanese: カーテンの隙間から射しこむ朝の陽が、頬や肩や首筋を撫でる冬の寒さが、白くまとわりつく眠気が、さえずる鳥の声が、布団の感触が、匂いが、大気が、重力が、俺たち自身が──
lines.english: The sunlight slipping between the curtains; the winter chill stroking cheek and shoulder and nape; the white drowse clinging around us; the birdsong; the touch of the bedding; its smell; the air; gravity; our very selves—

lines.japanese: ──あらゆるもの、俺たちを取りまくすべてが、あまりにも生々しく感じられた。
lines.english: —everything, every last thing surrounding us, felt almost unbearably vivid.

lines.japanese: タカシは──俺たちの中のタカシは──つまり俺はこう思った。たとえば近視のひとが初めて眼鏡をかけたとき、こんなふうに感じるんじゃないかな。
lines.english: Takashi—the Takashi within us, which is to say, I—thought this must be how a nearsighted person felt the first time they put on glasses.

lines.japanese: まざまざと見えすぎる世界を前にしたとき初めて、それまでの自分の視力が不自由であったことを知るんだって。そんな話をネットで読んだことがある。
lines.english: Only when the world came into almost excessive focus did you realize how impaired your sight had always been. I had read something like that online.

lines.japanese: 鷲介は──俺たちの中の鷲介は──つまり俺はこう言う。クオリアって言葉があるでしょう。
lines.english: Shusuke—the Shusuke within us, which is to say, I—said: You know the word *qualia*, right?

lines.japanese: 聴覚が鳥のさえずりを捕えたときに受けるあの感じ。目に光が飛びこんできたときのあの感じ。肌にシーツが擦れたときのあの感じ。要はその“感じ”ってのを、哲学や脳科学なんかではクオリアって言うらしいのよ。
lines.english: That feeling when your ears catch a bird's song. That feeling when light strikes your eyes. That feeling when a sheet brushes your skin. Apparently, philosophy and neuroscience call those *feelings* qualia.

lines.japanese: いま俺たちは、一人の全き人間として、本来得るべきクオリアを得ているのじゃないかしら。
lines.english: Perhaps now, as one whole human being, we were receiving the qualia we had always been meant to possess.

lines.japanese: 隼人は──俺たちの中の隼人は──つまり俺は嘲笑した。ハッ、知るかそんなん。クオリアだか氷屋だか知ンねーけど“感じ”なら“感じ”でいいじゃねえか。わざわざカッコ付けて横文字にすんじゃねえよ。
lines.english: Hayato—the Hayato within us, which is to say, I—scoffed. Hah. Who gives a shit? Qualia, koala—if you mean *feelings*, just call 'em feelings. Quit dressing it up in some fancy foreign word.

lines.japanese: 大体なんだァ？　本来得るべき氷屋を得ているゥ？　んだそりゃ。したらアレか。俺らみんな、今までは不完全だったっつーことか、おォ？
lines.english: And what the hell's that supposed to mean? We're finally getting the koala we were meant to have? So all of us were incomplete before now? That it?

lines.japanese: 伽楼羅は──俺たちの中の伽楼羅は──つまり俺は首肯した。しかり！　驕れるなかれ、ひとの子よ。世に生きとし生けるもの、みな不完全なるままに生まれ出づるのだ。恥じいるまでもない。
lines.english: Karura—the Karura within us, which is to say, I—nodded. Indeed! Be not proud, child of man. All living things are born incomplete. It is no cause for shame.

lines.japanese: 翻せば、ひとの歳を重ねたるは、すなわち完全を目指す行程ともいえる。なれば、いま我らは、歳若くしてその到達点を踏破したのだ。これは誇るべきことぞ。
lines.english: Looked at another way, the accumulating years of mortal life are a journey toward perfection. We have merely attained that destination while still young. This is a matter for pride.

lines.japanese: ヨージは──俺たちの中のヨージは──つまり俺は歓喜した。すっげー、なんか超すげぇー！　なんか超よく見えんの、音とかブワッてなるし、あとおれ超アタマ良くなっちった気ぃするよ。
lines.english: Yoji—the Yoji within us, which is to say, I—rejoiced. Awesome! This is super awesome! I can see everything so good, and the sounds all go *whoosh*, and I feel like I got super smart too!

lines.japanese: 誰かが──俺たちの中の誰かが──つまり俺は俺なのだから誰でもいいのだ──つまり俺は言った。
lines.english: Somebody—somebody within us, which is to say, I, and since I was I, it hardly mattered who—which is to say, I, spoke.

lines.japanese: 「始まったな、俺」
lines.english: “It's begun, me.”

lines.japanese: そして俺たちは──俺は、布団を撥ねのけ始まりの朝に立ちあがった。
lines.english: And we—I—threw off the covers and rose into the morning of beginnings.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう世界。ここからが第二幕だ」
lines.english: “Good morning, world. Act Two begins here.”

lines.japanese: 「こばとー？　小鳩いるかー、お兄ちゃんだぞう」
lines.english: “Kobato? You there, Kobato? It's your big brother.”

lines.japanese: 俺の中の誰かが疼くので、妹の部屋のふすまを軽く叩いた。しかし返事はない。
lines.english: Someone inside me ached to see her, so I tapped lightly on my sister's sliding door. There was no answer.

lines.japanese: 「ああ……まあ、そうか……」
lines.english: “Oh... Right. Of course...”

lines.japanese: ふすまを開け、無人の部屋を見渡しながら呟いた。
lines.english: I opened the door and murmured as I surveyed the empty room.

lines.japanese: 「この時間はもう下でパン食ってるよなあ、そりゃ」
lines.english: “Yeah, of course she's already downstairs eating bread by now.”

lines.japanese: 火曜日の朝。小鳩はもう登校準備を済ませて、居間で軽めの食事をとっているはず。むろん俺はそんなことなど知っている──
lines.english: Tuesday morning. Kobato would have finished getting ready for school and would be having a light breakfast in the living room. Naturally, I knew that—

lines.japanese: ──しかし、同時に知らないのだ。
lines.english: —and at the same time, I did not.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　知ってる？　けど知らない？　なんだこりゃ」
lines.english: “Hm? I know, but I don't? What's this about?”

lines.japanese: なんだこの矛盾した認識。
lines.english: What was this contradictory awareness?

lines.japanese: 家族の一員として当たり前に妹の生活サイクルを知っている一方で、こんなにも強く彼女を懐かしく思う気持ちも立ちうかんでいるんだ。
lines.english: Part of me knew my sister's routine as naturally as any member of her family. At the same time, another feeling welled up just as powerfully: a deep, aching nostalgia for her.

lines.japanese: 「クオリア……とか言ったっけ？」
lines.english: “Qualia... Was that the word?”

lines.japanese: 鷲介の言葉で語るなら、いまの俺は“羽田小鳩”を思う瞬間、いくつかの異なるクオリアを同時に得ていることになる。
lines.english: To put it in Shusuke's terms, the instant I thought of *Kobato Haneda*, I was receiving several distinct qualia at once.

lines.japanese: 毎日顔を合わせている馴染みぶかい家族。ときおり往来で遭遇するか弱い少女。暗黒の幽閉期間を経て久方ぶりの再会を果たしたばかりの愛しい姫君──
lines.english: A familiar member of the family I saw every day. A fragile girl I sometimes happened across in the street. A beloved princess with whom I had only just been reunited after a long imprisonment in darkness—

lines.japanese: ──そのどれもが、俺にとっての羽田小鳩らしい。
lines.english: —and every one of them, apparently, was Kobato Haneda to me.

lines.japanese: 一つのものに、五つの感想を持つ。考えればこの奇妙な混乱は、いま俺を取りまく一瞬一瞬の、あらゆる思考・感覚・体験に付いてまわっている。
lines.english: One thing, five impressions. Once I noticed it, this strange confusion accompanied every thought, sensation, and experience in each passing instant.

lines.japanese: 羽田家の廊下──見慣れた景色であり、見慣れない景色でもあり。
lines.english: The hallway of the Haneda home—at once a familiar sight and one I had never seen.

lines.japanese: 壁のスイッチ──照明の点灯装置であり、不思議な突起物でもあり。
lines.english: A switch on the wall—at once the mechanism that turned on the lights and a curious little protrusion.

lines.japanese: 学校──憂鬱を招くものでもあり、好奇心を煽るものでもあり。
lines.english: School—at once a source of gloom and a spur to curiosity.

lines.japanese: 「う……いちいち考えてたら脳味噌がパンクしそうだな」
lines.english: “Ugh... If I stop to think about every single thing, my brain's going to burst.”

lines.japanese: 俺たちは──俺は、偏頭痛にきしむこめかみを片手で撫でさすった。
lines.english: We—I—rubbed one temple as a migraine ground against it.

lines.japanese: やはり安易な統合など無茶だったのだと思う気持ち、大したことはないすぐに慣れるだろうと思う気持ち、難しいこと考えたくないから夢テレビでも見て誤魔化したいなあと思う気持ち。
lines.english: One part of me thought this hasty integration had been madness. One thought it was nothing serious, that we would soon adjust. And one did not want to think about anything difficult and wished to hide from it in Dream TV.

lines.japanese: 「ふう……とりあえず深く考えるのはやめよう。気楽に行こうじゃないか。ははは、いつも通りいつも通り」
lines.english: “Whew... Let's stop thinking too hard for now. We'll take it easy. Ha ha ha. Same as always, same as always.”

lines.japanese: 俺は居間へ向かう階段──同時に見知らぬ階段でもある──を、乗り物酔いでもしたような足取りで下りていった。
lines.english: I went down the stairs to the living room—which were also stairs I had never seen—staggering as if I were seasick.

lines.japanese: ところで……いつも通りって、どのいつも通りだ？
lines.english: But come to think of it... which *always* did I mean?

lines.japanese: 「あれ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 居間は無人だった。
lines.english: The living room was empty.

lines.japanese: ああ、今日は日直かなんかで普段より早めに家を出たのかな。
lines.english: Oh. Maybe she had some kind of morning duty and left earlier than usual.

lines.japanese: 舌先で頬の裏を撫でながら立ちつくす──
lines.english: I stood there, running the tip of my tongue along the inside of my cheek—

lines.japanese: ──と、見慣れた部屋の風景がたちまちその意味を失ってゆく。認識のゲシュタルト崩壊。次に気付いたとき、見慣れた部屋は見なれない部屋でもあった。
lines.english: —and suddenly, the familiar room lost its meaning. A Gestalt collapse of recognition. When I looked again, the room I knew was also one I did not know.

lines.japanese: 「ああもう、いちいち鬱陶しいっ！」
lines.english: “Oh, come on! This is getting obnoxious!”

lines.japanese: 俺たちは両手で頭を掴み、きつく目を閉ざした。
lines.english: We—I—clutched my head in both hands and squeezed my eyes shut.

lines.japanese: おい誰か、余計なクオリアを削ぎおとすにはどうすればいい？
lines.english: Somebody tell me: how do I strip away all the unnecessary qualia?

lines.japanese: そうだねえ誰かさん、いちばん強烈なクオリアをさらにさらに強く意識してみてはどうだろう。
lines.english: Well, whoever-you-are, why not concentrate even harder on whichever qualia feels strongest?

lines.japanese: 俺たちは意識を頭皮の裏に集中させ、この部屋に関してもっとも大きなクオリア──たぶんタカシの認識だろう──を大きく大きく膨らませる。
lines.english: We focused inward, just beneath the scalp, and swelled the strongest qualia associated with this room—Takashi's perception, presumably—larger and larger.

lines.japanese: ここは僕の家！　羽田の家の一室！　家族で食卓を囲む部屋！
lines.english: This is my home! A room in the Haneda house! The room where our family gathers around the table!

lines.japanese: 僕はここを知っている！　僕はここを知っている！　僕はここを知っている！
lines.english: I know this place! I know this place! I know this place!

lines.japanese: 俺たちはここを知っている！
lines.english: We know this place!

lines.japanese: 俺たちは──俺は、目を開けた。
lines.english: We—I—opened my eyes.

lines.japanese: そこは俺のよく知っている、長年のあいだ毎朝毎晩の食事をとってきた何でもないただの居間だった。
lines.english: It was the utterly ordinary living room I knew so well, where I had eaten breakfast and dinner every day for years.
“...Good.”

lines.japanese: この感覚だ。
lines.english: That was the feeling.

lines.japanese: こうしてクオリアが混濁しないよう自ら注力すれば──そして、この一連の思考動作を無意識に処理できるようにさえなれば、あの認識酔いとでも言うべき混乱を回避できるはず。
lines.english: If I made a conscious effort to keep the qualia from growing muddled—and if, eventually, I could process this whole chain of thought unconsciously—I ought to be able to avoid the confusion of what I could only call perceptual motion sickness.

lines.japanese: 「ふむ、ちょっと練習してみよう」
lines.english: “Hmm. Let's practice a little.”

lines.japanese: 俺はふたたび目蓋を下ろして腕を組んだ。
lines.english: I closed my eyes again and folded my arms.

lines.japanese: イメージする。
lines.english: I formed an image.

lines.japanese: タカシに関わるもの、鷲介に関わるもの、隼人に関わるもの。さまざまな物象をひとつずつイメージしては、その都度同時に浮かびあがってくる複数の認識を整理する。
lines.english: Things connected to Takashi. Things connected to Shusuke. Things connected to Hayato. I pictured different objects one by one, and each time I sorted through the multiple perceptions that surfaced together.

lines.japanese: 整理……できる。よし。
lines.english: I could... sort them. Good.

lines.japanese: 羽田家の居間は羽田タカシの住む邸宅の居間であって、それ以外の何物でもない。
lines.english: The Haneda living room was the living room of the home where Takashi Haneda lived, and nothing else.

lines.japanese: ひとつの物にひとつの認識。五人で見ても感想はひとつ。
lines.english: One object, one perception. Five observers, one impression.

lines.japanese: これだ。これを心がけていけば、たぶん、いける──何の根拠もないけれど。
lines.english: That was it. If I kept this up, it would probably work—though I had no basis for believing so.

lines.japanese: 仕方ない。統合したのは失敗だったなんて、簡単にあきらめるわけにもいかない。
lines.english: There was no other choice. I could not simply give up and declare our integration a mistake.

lines.japanese: 「玄関……うん、いつもの玄関だな。ただの玄関であり、珍しいものだと感じるクオリアは不要だ……」
lines.english: “The entryway... Yes, that's the usual entryway. Merely an entryway. I have no need for the qualia that make it feel unusual...”

lines.japanese: 「電話……これも見慣れてるものだ……新鮮に感じる必要はない、と……」
lines.english: “The telephone... Another familiar object... No need to find it fresh or novel...”

lines.japanese: 俺はひとつひとつ指差し確認しながら歩いた。
lines.english: I walked through the house, pointing at each thing and checking it off aloud.

lines.japanese: 俺の中の誰かは孤独な奈落生活が長かったせいで、独り言をこぼすという習慣が身についていた。
lines.english: Someone inside me had lived alone in the Abyss for so long that talking to himself had become a habit.

lines.japanese: 「これはカレンダーで……あれは造花……そんでこのドアは……ええと……」
lines.english: “This is a calendar... That's an artificial flower... And this door is... let's see...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、トイレか」
lines.english: “Oh. The bathroom.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、トイレはトイレだ。タカシの知っているトイレ。む、鷲介にも馴染みのある場所か……まあ、ここはタカシのクオリアを優先しておくとしよう」
lines.english: “Yes, the bathroom is the bathroom. The bathroom Takashi knows. Hm. A familiar place to Shusuke as well... We shall prioritize Takashi's qualia here.”
“Wh-what? What, what...?”

lines.japanese: 「んっ？　おまえは小鳩か。小鳩は小鳩。タカシの……いや、俺の妹。そう、俺の大事な妹だ。ふふふ、今日も俺の妹は可愛いなあ。うん、それからあれは便器。紛うことなき便器だ」
lines.english: “Hm? You're Kobato. Kobato is Kobato. Takashi's... no, my sister. Yes, my precious little sister. Heh heh. My sister is adorable today too. And that is a toilet bowl. An unmistakable toilet bowl.”

lines.japanese: 「なっ……ななな、なにを……」
lines.english: “Wh-what... What are you...”

lines.japanese: 「何を？　ああ、いまちょっと状況判断の調整中なんだ」
lines.english: “What am I doing? Oh, I'm just calibrating my grasp of the situation.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あああうああ……」
lines.english: “Ah... ahhh...”

lines.japanese: 「実は俺たち、さっき統合してな。まだいまいち勝手が掴めなくて、さしづめ試験運用中といったところだ。すぐには思考がまとまらない状態なんだが、なあに、五秒もあれば正確な認識把握が──」
lines.english: “The truth is, we integrated a little while ago. We haven't quite found our footing, so you might call this a trial run. I can't organize my thoughts immediately, but never fear. Give me five seconds and I will arrive at an accurate understanding—”

lines.japanese: 五秒後。
lines.english: Five seconds later.
“—Aaaah!?”

lines.japanese: 正確な認識把握をした俺は、いまこの瞬間が、呑気に兄弟の団欒などしている場合ではないことを悟った。
lines.english: Having arrived at an accurate understanding, I realized that this was no time for a leisurely moment between siblings.

lines.japanese: 「やっ！　あの！　ちが……ご、ごごごめっ」
lines.english: “I! Uh! This isn't—s-s-sorry!”

lines.japanese: 「ふぇ……ふえええ……」
lines.english: “Wah... waaah...”

lines.japanese: 「待て待て待て、泣くな！　ちちち、違うんだこれは、いいかよく聞け小鳩。あのな、おまえの大好きなお兄ちゃんはな……」
lines.english: “Wait, wait, wait! Don’t cry! Th-th-this isn’t what it looks like. Listen carefully, Kobato. Your beloved Big Brother, you see...”

lines.japanese: <8>\「ふえええええーん！」
lines.english: “Waaaaaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「うわあああ、ごめんなさあーあい！」
lines.english: “Waaaaah! I'm soooorry!”

lines.japanese: 俺はそのまま猛然と通学準備を済ませ、逃げるように家を飛びだした。
lines.english: I finished getting ready for school at furious speed and bolted out of the house as though fleeing for my life.

lines.japanese: ていうか逃げた。
lines.english: Actually, I ran away.

lines.japanese: ふう……あやうく変態兄貴の濡れ衣を着せられるところだった。
lines.english: Whew... I had very nearly been branded a pervert of a big brother.

lines.japanese: しかし幸いにも小鳩は聡明な子だ。この世に好き好んで妹を辱める兄などいない、そんなことぐらいは承知のはずだ。
lines.english: Fortunately, Kobato was a clever girl. Surely she understood that no brother in the world would willingly violate his own sister.

lines.japanese: 妹を辱める……兄など……。
lines.english: A brother who would... violate his own sister...

lines.japanese: 「いたじゃん！」
lines.english: “There was one!”

lines.japanese: 「てか俺じゃん！」
lines.english: “It was me!”

lines.japanese: あわわわ……。
lines.english: Oh, no...

lines.japanese: ヨージのやつ……ていうか俺のやつ……なんてことを……。
lines.english: Yoji—no, I—what had I done...?

lines.japanese: 「か、かかか、帰ったら土下座して謝らねば……」
lines.english: “Wh-when I get home, I have to get down on my knees and beg her forgiveness...”

lines.japanese: 俺は身震いしながら呟いた。
lines.english: I murmured through a shudder.

lines.japanese: 謝って済む問題ではない気もするが……ま、まあ、アレは分別のない子供のしたことだ、かわいい悪戯だと理解してくれる……。
lines.english: Though I had a feeling an apology would not settle the matter... W-well, that was the deed of a child too young to know better. She would understand it as an innocent little prank...

lines.japanese: いや、イタズラという言葉はよくないな。かえって語弊を招く。
lines.english: No. *Prank* was a dangerous word. It invited precisely the wrong impression.

lines.japanese: そう、決して遊びや悪戯であんなことをしたんじゃないんだ。そんないい加減な気持ちではなく、奈落の名にかけて、俺は真実彼女を愛しいと思ったからこそ──
lines.english: Yes. It had never been done lightly, as a game or prank. My feelings had been entirely sincere. Upon the name of the Abyss, I had acted only because I truly held her dear—

lines.japanese: 「なおダメじゃん……」
lines.english: “That's even worse...”

lines.japanese: なのに駄目だと分かっていながら、あのときのことを思うと胸に妙な鈍痛がよぎるのは何故だろう。
lines.english: Yet even knowing how wrong it had been, why did the memory send a strange, dull pain through my chest?

lines.japanese: もしかして、これは恋？
lines.english: Could this be love?

lines.japanese: 「反省の色なし！」
lines.english: “Not a trace of remorse!”

lines.japanese: あわわわ……。
lines.english: Oh, no...

lines.japanese: 「変態だ……俺の中に変態がいる……」
lines.english: “There's a degenerate inside me...”

lines.japanese: い、いや、違う。俺はまだ調整中なんだ。これもきっと無理な統合によって生じた精神的不具合だ。そう、それだ。
lines.english: N-no. That was wrong. I was still undergoing adjustment. This had to be a psychological malfunction caused by our forced integration. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: なにしろ俺たちは全員が全員、小鳩のことを大事に想っていた。その想いが五倍化しているだけの話。だけの話？　いや、ちょっと待て、それはわりと重大な問題なのでは……？
lines.english: After all, every one of us had cared deeply for Kobato. Those feelings had simply grown five times stronger. Simply? Wait. Wasn't that actually a fairly serious problem...?

lines.japanese: 頭を抱えて悶えながら突きすすむ俺たち──俺を、自転車を転がす住宅街の母子が怪訝そうな顔で見つめていた。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。
lines.english: As we—I—strode onward clutching my head in torment, a mother and child wheeling a bicycle down the residential street gave me a puzzled look. I'll fucking kill you, assholes.

lines.japanese: 「せせせ、世界が平和でありますように……」
lines.english: “*M-m-May peace prevail on Earth...*”
